prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your zip code, budget, schedule, brand preference, home size, and whether you want a national chain or a local specialist. I can help you pick one, but first a few quick questions:

- What is your Atlanta zip code or neighborhood?  
- Is this a single-family home, townhouse, or condo?  
- Do you know the age and tonnage of your current system, or the square footage of the house?  
- Any brand preferences (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc.) or budget range?  
- Do you need installation soon or just exploring options?

If you want a quick checklist and next steps while you decide, here’s what I recommend when choosing an installer:

Steps to find the right HVAC company
- Get at least 3 written quotes for a full replacement (not just a sales estimate).  
- Make sure the contractor performs a Manual J load calculation (correct sizing).  
- Confirm license and insurance — Georgia HVAC contractors must be licensed; ask for license number.  
- Look for technician certifications (NATE), and manufacturer dealer credentials (e.g., Trane Comfort, Carrier Factory Authorized).  
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and ask for local references.  
- Compare apples-to-apples: equipment model, SEER rating, warranty (parts and labor), permit costs, and removal of old unit.  
- Ask about energy-efficiency rebates and permit handling.  
- Request timeline, payment terms, and what’s included in start-up and warranty service.  

What to expect (ballpark)
- Typical full central AC replacements in Atlanta commonly fall in a wide range depending on system size and brand — often several thousand dollars to around $5,000–$12,000 for most homes. Exact cost depends on system size, efficiency (SEER), any ductwork repairs, and brand. Obtain multiple bids to narrow this.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and recommend 3–5 well-reviewed contractors near your zip code (with pros/cons), or  
- Give a sample list of questions to ask during estimates, or  
- Walk through interpreting quotes you already received.

Tell me your zip code and any preferences and I’ll pull a short vetted list for you.
